parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime nationally bars trans people from facilities matching their gender identity through the May 2025 restroom law and the April 2025 sexual-integrity law, which also reaches trans youth. This is a universal-exposure measure with no documented remedy that changes outcomes. Hate-crime and anti-discrimination protection on gender identity is not in force since the 2017 repeal. Offsetting positives are documented: the 2025 torture-by-discrimination conviction of police officers, the July 2025 annulment of an anti-equality decree, a conversion-therapy ban for professionals, and removal of pathologising health terminology. Visitor-facing custody, entry-document and violence magnitudes are not established. Rated in the elevated band.

entry_documents.exposure: No visitor-facing document rule for foreign-issued papers is documented. Domestic marker-change routes are resident-facing.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-country documents are not documented as checked against national gender markers at entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented detention or birth-sex custody placement of visitors. Vague child-protection articles and censorship-enabling provisions are documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Police officers convicted in 2025 for torture and sexual abuse of a trans woman, with sentences of 17 years.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility exclusion creates an entry point for stops or disputes, but no documented escalation to custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Nationally imposed bathroom restriction by birth sex (May 2025; April 2025 sexual-integrity law). Applies to all trans visitors in public facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Regional human-rights court advisory opinion cited, but not documented as operative against the restriction.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Universal and national, so it reaches visitors without local discretion. Oversight statements have not documented reversal.

care_services.exposure: Health-insurance classification uses 'gender discordance'. Emergency or routine visitor care denial is not documented.
care_services.protection: Conversion-therapy ban for medical professionals. Pathologising terminology removed from official guidance (June 2024).
care_services.interaction: Insurance classification is resident-facing; visitor care access is not documented either way.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Restroom laws frame trans people as harassment risks. Officials quoted with dehumanising comparisons. Public institutions documented as contributing to discrimination.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Capital court annulled an anti-equality decree (July 2025). Health ministry stated identity is not a disease.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing in law sits alongside judicial checks that have partly operated.

minors_guardians.exposure: April 2025 law bars trans youth from facilities matching identity. A travelling minor and guardian would face the same restriction and possible disputes in public facilities.
minors_guardians.protection: Age of consent set equally for trans and cisgender youth (2012). Conversion-therapy ban covers minors via professionals.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardians travelling with a trans minor may be drawn into facility disputes under the restriction.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Hate crimes reported as rising with trans women most affected. Recorded figures are a sub-registry with no denominator, so magnitude relative to background violence is undetermined. Public harassment of a legislator is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Conviction of police for torture-by-discrimination (2025) shows a prosecutorial route. Pride marches held annually since 2002.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: The conviction took nearly 20 years, so recourse is slow and was documented only in one major case.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Hate-crime and anti-discrimination coverage on gender identity is not in force since 2017. The April 2025 NGO foreign-funding law could be weaponised against queer organising.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Regional court route exists. Constitutional challenges have succeeded in part (July 2025).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse is largely judicial and slow, and the legislature has repeatedly moved against protections.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a border registry and entry refusals for trans visitors, which is a harsher traveller-facing exclusion than the bathroom restriction here. This dossier has no documented entry refusal, so it sits above 0.35-A.

0.45-D combines universal registration with hotel data sharing and documented harassment and eviction. This dossier documents universal facility exclusion and no hate-crime coverage, but no registration or eviction, so it is similar in tier and the two sit near each other.

0.55-C documents ward placement by birth-sex documents, with delayed care and partial denial. This dossier documents facility exclusion but no ward or custody placement by birth sex, and it has a documented torture conviction and conversion-therapy ban, so it sits somewhat below 0.55-C.

parsed.synthesis: The national bathroom restriction by birth sex is a universal exposure that reaches every trans visitor, including trans minors travelling with guardians, and no enforced remedy is documented. Anti-discrimination and hate-crime protection on gender identity is absent, and the state has framed trans people as threats. Against this, the 2025 torture-by-discrimination conviction, the annulment of an anti-equality decree, and the conversion-therapy ban show that courts and some institutions can act. Visitor-facing custody, entry-document practice and the true magnitude of violence are undetermined, so the rating stays in the elevated band.
